subject: Physics
question: A ball is thrown horizontally at 12.0 m s⁻¹ from the top of a building 45.0 m high. Calculate the time it takes to reach the ground and the horizontal distance it travels. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻².
response_text:
Vertical motion: u_y = 0, s_y = 45.0 m, g = 9.81 m s⁻².
s_y = ½gt² ⇒ t = √(2s_y/g) = √(2 × 45.0 / 9.81) = 3.03 s
(t is a time, so only the positive root is taken.)
Horizontal motion: u_x = 12.0 m s⁻¹ and there is no horizontal acceleration, so
x = u_x t = 12.0 × 3.03 = 36.4 m
The ball lands about 36 m from the base of the building after roughly 3.0 s.

correct_steps: about 36 m from the base of the building after roughly 3.0 s
